chunks: Among his proofs (peace be upon him) is that he said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not make for people in their deeds any proof except through an Imam who guides them to the path of success, and teaches them what they did not know from the affairs of their religion, and prohibits for them what Allah prohibited for them, and makes permissible for them what Allah made permissible for them.

key_terms.إِمَام: Imam, the divinely appointed guide and leader
key_terms.حُجَّة: Proof or argument establishing divine authority
key_terms.سَبِيلُ الرَّشَادِ: The path of success or guidance

ai.seo_question: Why is an Imam necessary for Muslims to have a valid proof in their religious deeds?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this hadith within the doctrine of *Ismah* (infallibility), emphasizing that the Imam is not merely a political leader but the indispensable *Hujjah* (proof) of God upon earth, ensuring the continuity of divine guidance after the Prophet. This establishes the Imam as the living interpreter of the Quran and the source of authoritative *halal* and *haram*, a concept central to Shia Usul al-Din. The narration underscores that without this divinely appointed guide, the transmission and understanding of religious law would be subject to human error and alteration.
